messages:
matt: quick q — we should add a per-token drilldown on the cost dashboard, but worried about query perf. ideas?

tara: yes please. the ask from product was: click a route -> see token-level breakdown (model vs cache vs overhead) for last 24h. needs hovercards, sorting, and export.

kevin: naive agg is heavy if we pull raw tokens. we currently sample ~1% at ingest for detailed traces. full-resolution exists for 7 days only.

liza: what if UI shows sampled view by default and a "full rez" button that triggers an async job and email when ready? keeps dashboard snappy.

matt: that could work. UX question: how to surface cache savings attribution? per-invocation savings can be negative when prefetch warms incorrectly.

tara: show two lines: observed token cost and amortized cost (with amortization window). annotate negative-savings with tooltip: "cache warmed by previous requests".

kevin: backend note: we need additional rollup keys: model_sku, model_variant, route_id, cache_fingerprint. that'll blow up cardinality unless we pre-aggregate.

matt: pre-agg proposal: hourly rollups by (route_id, model_sku, is_cached_flag) plus counters for token_count, cached_token_count, compute_tokens, kv_reads. cheap to store and easy to compute per-token cost.

liza: +1. for drilldown we can show provenance links to sample traces stored in trace_store (sample ids). UI: small "view samples" action next to each row.

kevin: implementation detail: amortized cache credit needs prefetched_token_count and a window size. we'll add fields: amort_window_hours and prefetch_owner.

matt: is changing telemetry schema backwards-compatible? some customers read these columns directly.

kevin: we'll default new fields nullable. old queries shouldn't break. but console SQL panels that SELECT * will get new cols — note in release notes.

tara: rollout plan: feature flag on console; enable internally for a week; gather perf metrics (panel load time, backend query duration). then gradual for 10% tenants.

liza: UX polish: allow toggling between sampled/full and a little cost-impact mini-chart inline showing "estimated extra billing if full."

matt: good. question: do we surface per-model unit economics (cost per token per model) or per-route effective cost? product wants both.

kevin: we can compute per-model unit cost from rollups: cost_per_compute_token = compute_cost / compute_tokens. then route effective = weighted average plus cache credits. cheap.

matt: ok i'll sketch API changes. sample snippet for the rollup query we want in telemetry service:

```sql
SELECT route_id, model_sku, is_cached, sum(token_count) as token_count, sum(compute_tokens) as compute_tokens, sum(kv_reads) as kv_reads, sum(cost_usd) as cost_usd, avg(amort_window_hours) as amort_window
FROM telemetry_rollups.hourly
WHERE ts BETWEEN $start AND $end
GROUP BY route_id, model_sku, is_cached
```

tara: add a pre-aggregated materialized view for last 7d that the console reads. keeps dashboard snappy.

kevin: agree. I'll prototype the schema changes and compute lambda. estimate ~2 days to add fields + mv + API.

liza: I'll mock the UI interaction in Figma and drop screens here when ready.

matt: can cost-bot run a quick sim on how many rollup rows this adds for our busiest shard?

cost-bot: sim: busiest shard: ~3.2M unique (route_id x model_sku) per day -> rollup rows/day ~3.2M (hourly -> ~76.8M rows for 24h). materialized view reduces reads by 95% for dashboard patterns.

matt: that scale is high but manageable with MV + TTL. thanks. next steps: kevin implement schema + mv, liza mock, tara coordinate flag + rollout checks. I'll open a PR for the console panel.

kevin: filing telemetry PR today.

liza: will ping design drop in ~48h.

tara: added to rollout calendar. tagging @eng-oncall in case of unexpected perf.

matt: perfect. short follow-up: include an opt-out for customers who don't want sampled traces stored (privacy). we'll add a tenant opt-out flag.

kevin: noted.

matt: thanks all :thumbsup:
